name: Aeneas
role: Trojan hero and ancestor of the Roman people
fun_fact: Virgil's Aeneid ends not with the founding of Rome but with Aeneas killing Turnus, leaving the city's future to his descendants.

name: Romulus
role: Twin founder and first king of Rome
fun_fact: Roman tradition dated the founding of Rome to 753 BCE and made Romulus its first king and lawgiver.

name: Remus
role: Twin brother of Romulus and rival founder
fun_fact: Remus is said to have seen six vultures while Romulus saw twelve, a dispute over augury that ended in his death.

name: Mars
role: God of war and father of Romulus and Remus
fun_fact: Mars was originally also an agricultural god, and his spring festivals were tied to the fertility of fields and herds.

name: Venus
role: Goddess of love and mother of Aeneas
fun_fact: Julius Caesar claimed descent from Venus through Aeneas, making the goddess a political ancestor of his family.

name: Juno
role: Queen of the gods and protector of Rome
fun_fact: Juno was worshipped on the Capitol as Juno Moneta, 'the Warner', and her temple gave its name to the Roman mint.

name: Ceres
role: Goddess of grain, harvest and agriculture
fun_fact: The Cerealia festival honoured Ceres, and her name survives in the English word cereal.

name: Proserpina
role: Queen of the underworld and goddess of spring
fun_fact: Proserpina is the Roman counterpart of the Greek Persephone; her return from the underworld marked the beginning of spring.

name: Cupid
role: God of desire and son of Venus
fun_fact: In Apuleius' story Cupid is a hidden husband rather than a chubby child, and his union with Psyche becomes an allegory of the soul.

name: Psyche
role: Mortal woman who becomes the bride of Cupid
fun_fact: The Greek word psyche means both 'soul' and 'butterfly', and later art often gives Psyche butterfly wings.
